text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English explorer of the Antarctic, SIR JAMES CLARK ROSS, was born in 1800.
American novelist HENRY JAMES was born in 1843.
Australian cricketer DAVID GREGORY, who captained our first team to tour England (20 of his descendents have played for NSW), was born in 1845.
Australian Prime Minister STANLEY BRUCE was born in 1883.
American singer BESSIE SMITH (considered by many to have been the finest female blues singer ever) was born in 1894.
Italian actress CLAUDIA CARDINALE (who appeared in many films including 'The Pink Panther' and 'Once Upon A Time In The West') was born in 1939.

British model/singer SAMANTHA FOX was born in 1966. She came to prominence primarily through her topless modelling. She had subsequent hits such as "Touch Me" (1986), "Do Ya Do Ya" (1986), "Nothing's Gonna Stop Me Now" (1987), "Naughty Girls" (1988) and "I Only Wanna Be With You" (1989).
UK bassist, songwriter and singer from 'Wet, Wet, Wet' GRAEME CLARK was born in 1966.
** EVENTS **
1450 : The French defeated the English at the Battle of
Formigny in the last phase of the 100 Years' War.
1753 : Dr SAMUEL JOHNSON published his Dictionary, which
took 9 years to compile.
1865 : President ANDREW JOHNSON was sworn in, following
the assassination of ABRAHAM LINCOLN.
1912 : The White Star passenger liner Titanic sank on her
maiden voyage after hitting an iceberg off Newfoundland; 1,523 of the 2,200 passengers and crew lost their lives in the supposedly unsinkable vessel.
1925 : SIR JAMES BARRIE donated the copyright of "Peter
Pan" to the Great Ormond Street Hospital For Sick Children in London.
1925 : American painter JOHN SINGER SARGENT died in
London.
1942 : The British government banned embroidery on
women's underwear and nightwear as a war-time economy measure.
1942 : The George Cross, Britain's highest accolade for
civilian gallantry, was conferred on Malta by King GEORGE VI for bravery in withstanding Italian and German attacks.
1945 : Looted Nazi art treasures, including paintings by
RUBENS, GOYA, RAPHAEL and LEONARDO DA VINCI, were found hidden away in an Austrian mineshaft.
1955 : The first MCDONALDS hamburger store opened, in San
Bernardino, California.
1971 : British and Chinese governments agreed to the
reopening of a telephone link between London and Shanghai which had been closed for 22 years.
1980 : French philosopher, novelist and poet JEAN-PAUL
SARTRE died. He was awarded, but declined to accept, the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1964.
1986 : United States aircraft bombed the Presidential
Palace of Libyan leader Colonel GADDAFI, in retaliation for a Libyan attack on an American radar base in Italy. GADDAFI's 15 month old adopted daughter was killed in the attack.
1989 : 95 people were crushed to death and another 200

were injured at Hillsborough Stadium in Sheffield. Liverpool and Nottingham Forest were about to play an FA CUP semi-final when thousands of fans (who'd arrived just before kick-off) when suddenly let into the stadium, crushing those already in the stand.
1990 : Legendary actress GRETA GARBO (GRETA LOVISA
GUSTAFSSON) died in New York after almost half a century of self-imposed isolation. The daughter of an unskilled Swedish labourer, she was taken to Hollywood in 1925 by Russian director

MAURITZ STILLER. She first appeared in silent films ("The Torrent" 1926) and later appeared in the 'talkies' including "Mata Hari" (1931), "Grand Hotel" (1932), "Anna Karenina" (1935) and "Ninotchka" (1939). She retired in 1941, believing "the creative artist should be a rare and solitary spirit".
1994 : African National Congress leader NELSON MANDELA
and South African President F.W. de KLERK took part in the country's first-ever televised political debate in the lead-up to historic all-race elections.
1994 : Ministers from the world's trading nations signed
the GATT pact (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade), the biggest market-opening treaty in history.
1996 : South Africa's "truth commission", looking into
abuses during the apartheid era, began its public hearings.
1996 : Japan and the U.S. announced the closure of six
more U.S. military facilities on the southern Japanese island of Okinawa, reducing the amount of land occupied by American forces there by a fifth.
